text: Checkup with Dr. Reyes today. Sam's HbA1c is down to 6.4. She kept metformin at 500 mg twice a day and did not add anything new.
Ana stopped taking omeprazole two weeks ago because the reflux cleared up. She is still on levothyroxine 50 mcg every morning.
The cardiologist talked about starting Leo on a statin but decided against it for now; they'll recheck cholesterol in six months.
Allergy panel results: Ana is not allergic to penicillin after all. The rash last year was viral. She is allergic to cats and dust mites.
Bob thinks he might be lactose intolerant, but he hasn't been tested yet.
Sam's doctor increased the lisinopril from 10 mg to 20 mg because her blood pressure was still high.
Leo was diagnosed with mild asthma as a kid but hasn't needed an inhaler in over ten years.
Ana's sister was just diagnosed with celiac disease. Ana got tested too and her results were negative.
Bob finished his ten-day course of amoxicillin for the sinus infection yesterday.
Note for Sam: avoid ibuprofen with the kidney issue; paracetamol is fine for headaches.
Leo started sertraline 50 mg in January. The psychiatrist wants to keep the dose the same through the summer.
Ana's thyroid ultrasound showed a small nodule, probably benign; the endocrinologist wants a biopsy to rule out cancer.
Bob is no longer on atorvastatin; he switched to rosuvastatin 10 mg because of muscle aches.
Sam told me her mother takes warfarin, so she worries about bleeding risk running in the family. Sam herself takes no blood thinners.
The ER doctor suspected appendicitis but the CT scan ruled it out; Leo was sent home with gastroenteritis.
Ana has been vegetarian since 2019 and takes a B12 supplement three times a week.
Bob's peanut allergy is severe; he carries two EpiPens. His son has no known allergies.
Sam may try melatonin for sleep if the new routine doesn't help, but she hasn't started it.
Leo's blood type came back as B positive, not A positive like the old clinic record said.
After the gastric sleeve, Ana stopped metformin entirely; her glucose has been normal for three months without it.
